items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PDL-CUL-25-002, Reimagining Doon and Village Infrastructure Project Updates
notes:
C. Huinink expressed appreciation for the accessibility modifications prior to the reopening of the museum and requested that Staff incorporate accessibility history. Julian Kingston, Director of Cultural Services, confirmed that Staff will be working with community to develop the broadest palette of history for Doon. 
P. Wolf expressed her disappointment that the Doon and Village will not be reopening in 2025. She noted that Doon and the Waterloo Regional Heritage Foundation have taken time to reset to respect diversity and inclusion. She further noted that she believes that by taking the pause to review their strategic priorities that these organizations have been penalized by not reopening or being given funding.

 
Received for information.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
CSD-SEN-25-001, Sunnyside Home Medical Director’s Report 2024
notes:
Julie Wheeler, Director, Seniors' Services, introduced Dr. Fred Mather, Sunnyside Home Medical Director, to provide a presentation. Dr. F. Mather spoke to the work that has been done at Sunnyside Home with respect to infection prevention and control, quality improvement, and supporting care partners through palliative care. He highlighted the benefits of vaccination programs and antiviral treatments with mitigating Covid-19, and noted that they are also monitoring RSV and Influenza. Dr. Mather explained changes that have been made to palliative care and discussions with individuals to have advanced planning to ensure that there is informed consent for treatment.

The Committee acknowledged the good works of Dr. Mather and all the Staff at Sunnyside.

In response to the Committee, Dr. Mather highlighted several important considerations for integrated palliative care such as continuity in long term care facilities with primary care. He further highlighted that nurse practitioners have a major impact in long term care facilities as models of care change. Sunnyside has a nurse practitioner in the home from Monday to Friday that is able to provide support to physicians and the registered staff. The additional support is essential as residents are coming into the home with more complex issues and more clinician presence is necessary.

Responding to the Committee, Dr. Mather confirmed that the medical assistance in dying (MAID) program is used, however, because many residents in long term care facilities have cognitive considerations it is difficult to ensure consent to utilize the MAID program. 

J. Wheeler recognized the increasing demands for care in the community for older adults and the next steps that are needed to move forward. Staff will be developing a 10 year plan for senior services and the Sunnyside campus.

Regional Chair K. Redman thanked Dr. F. Mather on behalf of Council for his leadership and service to the Region and the Long Term Care sector.

Received for information.
